form:FormGroup.helpText: Whether the model is offered this server's tools. A disabled server is kept, but not connected to.

form:FormGroup.label: Name
form:FormGroup.helpText: A short name for this tool server. It is shown to users, starts the names of its tools as the model sees them (e.g. 'fastmcp__find_feeds'), and appears in error messages.

g:TextBox.title: A short name for this tool server.

form:FormGroup.label: Endpoint URL
form:FormGroup.helpText: The server's MCP Streamable HTTP endpoint, e.g. https://mcp.example.com/mcp . Both http and https are supported; use https for anything not on the same machine.

g:TextBox.title: The MCP Streamable HTTP endpoint URL.

form:FormGroup.label: Authentication
form:FormGroup.helpText: How Stroom proves who it is to the server. 'OAuth2 passthrough' signs each user in to the server, so the server acts as them: with an external identity provider it sends the user's own sign-in token; with Stroom's internal identity provider it sends a short-lived token Stroom issues (see Token audience). The other modes send one stored credential for everyone.

form:FormGroup.label: Credential
form:FormGroup.helpText: The stored credential to authenticate with. For 'Bearer token' and 'Custom API key header' this is an Access Token credential; for 'Basic auth' it is a Username / Password credential.

form:FormGroup.label: API key header name
form:FormGroup.helpText: The HTTP header to send the key in, e.g. X-API-Key. Default: Authorization

g:TextBox.title: The HTTP header to send the key in.

form:FormGroup.label: API key value prefix
form:FormGroup.helpText: Text placed before the key in the header, e.g. 'Bearer ' (with its trailing space). Leave empty to send the key on its own.

g:TextBox.title: An optional prefix placed before the key value.

form:FormGroup.label: Token audience
form:FormGroup.helpText: Stroom uses its internal identity provider, so for 'OAuth2 passthrough' it issues each user a short-lived token for this server, with this audience, e.g. stroom-mcp. Configure the server with Stroom's issuer, its JWKS URL and this audience. For the server to call Stroom back as the user, also add the audience to stroom.security.authentication.openId.allowedAudiences. Tokens are only sent to a trusted server over https (or on the same machine).

g:TextBox.title: The audience of the tokens Stroom issues for this server.

form:FormGroup.helpText: Whether you trust this server, e.g. because you run it. Only a trusted server's tool descriptions (such as 'read-only') are believed, so its read-only tools can run without asking. Every tool of an untrusted server asks the user before running, unless a policy below says otherwise.

form:FormGroup.label: Tool policies
form:FormGroup.helpText: What happens when the model wants to use a tool. Each policy has a regular expression that must match the tool's whole name, ignoring case, e.g. 'find_.*' or '(get|list)_feeds?'. The first policy that matches a tool applies: Allow runs it without asking, Ask every time asks the user each time, and Deny never offers it to the model. A tool no policy matches runs without asking if the server is trusted and the tool is read-only, and otherwise asks.
